thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: increased 5xx rate from canary-3 in eu-west-1 for /v1/generate — 78% errors over 2m. Deploy ref: release/2026-03-15-canary. Triggered autoscaler events.
Alice: I saw the pager. Is this the canary we pushed at 10:30?
Carla: yes, that canary included the new autoscaler / HPA config change and the drain-friendly eviction policy.
Ben (oncall): I'm taking the page. brief status: 5xx spike + pods CrashLoopBackOff on canary-3 replica set. Investigating logs now.
Ben (oncall): running `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=canary-3 -o wide`
Ben (oncall): ```
NAME                          READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
canary-3-5b7f9c8f6-abcde      0/1     CrashLoopBackOff   4          4m
canary-3-5b7f9c8f6-fghij      1/1     Running            0          9m
```
Dmitri: there's also node pressure on node-ip-10-4-7-22 from multiple evictions earlier. HPA may be too aggressive with target 70% CPU — combined with new init that spikes CPU, it thrashes.
Alice: can we pause rollout / flip kill switch on the flag? If this is customer-impacting we should halt.
Carla: I can flip the feature flag for canary traffic to 0% via the release service. Command: `POST https://release.internal/flags/canary-traffic {"percent":0}`
Ben (oncall): Doing quick rollback of the ReplicaSet to previous replicaset (rs-20260314) to stop the failing pods. `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/canary-3 --to-revision=3`
Eva (support): Customers are starting to file errors. ETA for mitigation? Customers: 6 enterprise tenants in eu-west.
Ben (oncall): Rollback initiated. Watching rollout status: `kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/canary-3 --watch`
Ben (oncall): Rollback shows new pods coming up, but node had `NotReady` taint after drain attempt. Running `kubectl describe node node-ip-10-4-7-22`
Ben (oncall): ```
Name: node-ip-10-4-7-22
Conditions: Ready=False (KubeletNotReady)
Taints: node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule
Allocated resources: memory pressure
```
Dmitri: That node got cordoned during a maintenance drain, but some pods were forced evicted earlier and never rescheduled due to the HPA surge. I'll uncordon and try to reprovision. `kubectl uncordon node-ip-10-4-7-22`
Dmitri: Uncordoned. Kubelet still showing NotReady, looks like a kernel OOM-fallback from the init spike. Rebooting node via cloud provider.
Carla: Flag flip confirmed: canary traffic -> 0%. :white_check_mark: That should cut new customer impact while rollback finishes.
Eva (support): Notifying affected customers and setting expectations: "We've identified a canary rollout issue causing elevated 5xx in eu-west. Traffic has been routed away from the canary and we're rolling back. We'll update in 15m."
Alice: Good. Ben, any signs the rollback completed?
Ben (oncall): Rollout now at 100% stable replicas of rs-20260314, newest pods are Running. Monitoring metrics — 5xx dropping to baseline but still some errors from existing connections.
Ben (oncall): Confirming HPA: it currently has minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=20, targetCPU=70. We should lower targetCPU to 50 for short-term to avoid aggressive scale-ups until init spike is addressed.
Carla: I'll prepare a quick manifest patch and a canary rollback plan + follow-up task to revert HPA change after we fix init behavior.
Carla: Patch diff (will apply to k8s):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: canary-3-hpa
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 50
```
Ben (oncall): Applied HPA patch. `kubectl apply -f canary-hpa-tmp.yaml` — HPA target now 50. Watching for oscillation.
Dmitri: Node reboot is done, kubelet back to Ready, previously evicted pods are re-scheduled.
Ben (oncall): 5xx rate at 1.8% now, back to normal for eu-west. No new crashloops. Rolling back the canary deployment and feature flag flip seems to have prevented further customer impact.
Alice: Nice containment. Next: create a post-incident task to root-cause the init spike + HPA thresholds + node maintenance coordination. Assign to infra + ML infra.
Carla: I'll create the incident ticket and include timeline, kubectl outputs, and the temporary HPA patch + the flag change. Tagging Dmitri and Alice.
Eva (support): Sent customer follow-up note to the six tenants, offering incident summary & status.
Ben (oncall): Handing off to Ben (oncall) -> Alice for postmortem. I'll stay available for 10 more mins then go offline.
Alice: Taking handoff. Please include any logs that show the init CPU spike (container init logs).
Dmitri: I grabbed the kubelet and node system logs and uploaded to /artifacts/incidents/1863009876.
Carla: Planned actions for postmortem: 1) Reproduce init CPU spike locally with canary image, 2) Adjust HPA rules for cold-start scenarios, 3) Improve node drain playbook to avoid cordoning while maintenance in progress, 4) Add chaos test for rolling updates + HPA.
Alice: Thanks team. Closing timeline: incident declared at 1863009876, rollback + flag flip at 1863009898, HPA patch at 1863009920, node recovered at 1863009935, incident resolved at 1863009950. Will open a formal postmortem doc. :spiral_notepad:"
